etymologies.bridge: From brigge, from brycġ bridge, from gmw-pro *bruggju, from gem-pro *brugjō, gem-pro *brugjǭ t=bridge, from ine-pro *bʰerw-, ine-pro *bʰrēw- t=wooden flooring, decking, bridge. 2 Cognate with , t=bridge, t=bridge, , Bröch t=bridge, Brääch, Brääg t=bridge, brêge t=bridge, t=bridge, Brücke t=bridge, brögk t=bridge, Bréck t=bridge, t=bridge, בריק t=bridge, -, brygge t=jetty, pier, wharf, -, bryggja t=pier, brygge, bryggje t=jetty, pier, wharf, brygga t=bridge; pier. The verb is from briggen, from brycġian to bridge, make a causeway, pave, derived from the noun.
etymologies.capacitor: :af capacity -or text=++ Capacitor replaced the term condenser (coined by Alessandro Volta in 1782) to disambiguate it from steam condenser. The coiner is unknown but the change was recommended in 1926 by British Standard Glossary of Terms in Electrical Engineering.
etymologies.choke: From choken (also cheken), from earlier acheken, from āċēocian to choke, probably derived from ċēoce, ċēace jaw, cheek, see . Cognate with throat, to gulp. See also achoke.
etymologies.circuit: From circuit, from circuit, from circuitus a going round, from circuire go round, from circum around + .
etymologies.circumference: ine-pro *(s)ker- (turn) *bʰer- From circumferentia, from circum around + ferō to carry. Displaced native ymbgang.
etymologies.flip-flop: . Most probably an imitation of the sound produced when walking in them.
etymologies.group: :bor fr:groupe :bor it:gruppo From groupe, from gruppo, groppo. Displaced native tribe, group. In the "group theory" sense, calque#Verb calqued from groupe, a term coined by the young French mathematician Évariste Galois in 1830.
etymologies.itineration: From itinerate -ion, ultimately borrowed from la-med itinerātiō, from itineror, from itiner-.
etymologies.journey: ine-pro *dyew- From journe, from jornee, from la-vul *diurnāta, from la-lat diurnum, from diurnus, from . Displaced native and .
etymologies.lap: From lappe, from læppa, from gmw-pro *lappō, from gem-pro *lappô, of origin, possibly ine-pro *leb-. Cognate with , Lappen, leppur.
etymologies.link: From linke, lenke, from a merger of hlenċe, hlenċa ring; chainlink and *hlenkr, hlekkr ring; chain; both from gem-pro *hlankiz ring; bond; fettle; fetter, from gem-pro *hlankaz, from ine-pro *kleng-, ine-pro *klenk-. Used in English since the 14th century. Related to .
etymologies.locomotion: ine-pro *m(y)ewh₁- From locomotion, from (ablative of locus) + mōtiōnem motion, a moving (nominative mōtio), from moveō movēre, from ine-pro *m(y)ewh₁-.
etymologies.path: ine-pro *pent- From , , from path, track, from gmw-pro *paþ, from gem-pro *paþaz. The Proto-Germanic term is possibly borrowed from , from ira-pro *pántaHs, from iir-pro *pántaHs, from ine-pro *póntoh₁s, from the root ine-pro *pent-, but this is disputed. 2 Cognate with Paad, Pad, , , Pfad, nds-de Padd, Pad.
etymologies.pub crawl: From the fact that the participants are supposed to be unable to stand up straight by the end of the event.
etymologies.relay: :der frm:relai From relai reserve pack of hounds, from relaier to exchange tired animals for fresh; literally, "to leave behind", from relaier to leave behind, from re- + laier to leave, of uncertain origin.
